hints: Focus on where the Br adds to the C=C bond, the major product follows the most stable carbocation.
Draw 2-methylbut-2-ene as $(CH_3)_2C=CHCH_3$ and work out that H adds to C-3 to give a tertiary carbocation at C-2.
Remember that $R-Br$ to $R-CN$ to $R-COOH$ keeps the same carbon skeleton but adds one extra carbon as the $COOH$ carbon.
walkthrough:
**Identify the starting alkene and the HBr addition**

Think of methylbut-2-ene as 2-methylbut-2-ene, $(CH_3)_2C=CHCH_3$. HBr adds electrophilically across the double bond.

$$ (CH_3)_2C=CHCH_3 + HBr \rightarrow \text{bromoalkane X} $$

**Apply Markovnikov to find X**

$H^+$ adds to the $CH$ carbon to form the more stable tertiary carbocation at C-2, then $Br^-$ attacks there. This gives 2-bromo-2-methylbutane as the major product.

$$ (CH_3)_2C=CHCH_3 + H^+ / Br^- \rightarrow (CH_3)_2CBrCH_2CH_3 $$

**Convert bromide to nitrile to add one carbon**

$CN^-$ from KCN substitutes for $Br$ by nucleophilic substitution. The skeleton stays the same, but the nitrile carbon is new.

$$ (CH_3)_2CBrCH_2CH_3 + CN^- \rightarrow (CH_3)_2C(CN)CH_2CH_3 + Br^- $$

**Hydrolyse the nitrile to the carboxylic acid**

Acid hydrolysis converts $-CN$ into $-COOH$ with the same carbon now as C-1 of the acid. Counting $COOH$ as C-1 gives two methyl branches on C-2 of a butanoic acid chain.

$$ (CH_3)_2C(CN)CH_2CH_3 + 2H_2O + H^+ \rightarrow (CH_3)_2C(COOH)CH_2CH_3 + NH_4^+ $$

**Name compound Z**

The structure $(CH_3)_2C(COOH)CH_2CH_3$ is 2,2-dimethylbutanoic acid, which matches the chain extension logic.

options.A: Correct. Markovnikov addition gives $(CH_3)_2CBrCH_2CH_3$, substitution gives $(CH_3)_2C(CN)CH_2CH_3$, and hydrolysis gives $(CH_3)_2C(COOH)CH_2CH_3$. With $COOH$ as C-1, this is 2,2-dimethylbutanoic acid.
options.B: Incorrect. This is the anti-Markovnikov trap. It would form if $H^+$ added to the more substituted carbon to give the secondary carbocation $(CH_3)_2CHC^+HCH_3$, leading to 3-bromo-2-methylbutane and then to 2,3-dimethylbutanoic acid. The major product uses the tertiary carbocation instead.
options.C: Incorrect. 2-methylpentanoic acid is a skeletal isomer with the $COOH$ on a different carbon framework, $CH_3CH_2CH_2CH(CH_3)COOH$. It does not match the tertiary bromide skeleton $(CH_3)_2CBrCH_2CH_3$ extended by one $CN$ carbon.
options.D: Incorrect. 3-methylpentanoic acid, $CH_3CH_2CH(CH_3)CH_2COOH$, would place the methyl branch on C-3 of the acid. Our product has both methyls on the carbon next to $COOH$ (C-2) because the $C-Br$ and then $C-CN$ carbon becomes C-2 of the acid.
